title: The share of US households with one person doubled after 1960
body: The US census recorded one-person households at 13.3% of households in 1960 and 27.6% in 2020. The figures count households rather than the share of Americans who live alone.
takeaway: A population can require more homes per person as its households become smaller.
source: US Census Bureau, Households and Families: 2020

title: About one in five young people were out of work and education in 2023
body: The International Labour Organization estimated that 20.4% of people worldwide aged 15 to 24 were outside employment, education and training in 2023. The figure includes young people who were not actively seeking work.
takeaway: Counting unemployment alone leaves out people who have stopped looking or never started.
source: International Labour Organization, Global Employment Trends for Youth 2024

title: A Chicago summer jobs offer cut violent-crime arrests in a trial
body: Sara Heller and colleagues studied summer job offers made by lottery to young people in Chicago. Their 2017 analysis of two trials found fewer violent-crime arrests after the offer, without a sustained rise in employment.
takeaway: An employment programme can affect what happens away from the workplace even when its job effects are limited.
